thread:
Anika: Thinking about a compact 'filter shelf' in Console analytics — a horizontal strip of selectable pills (route, model, tag, env) you can stack and collapse. Idea is faster ad-hoc compares without opening the full sidebar. Mobile-friendly. Thoughts?
Ryan: I like the shelf idea. Could be great for quick toggles. Concern: do we persist the shelf per-user or per-view?
Jess: Persist per-user by default, but allow saving as a 'compact view' to share. Saved views already exist but are heavy — this is lightweight.
Tim: UX nit: when you stack pills, you want to know which are pinned to route vs global. Maybe pill color or a little lock icon for view-scoped filters.
Anika: Agreed. Pinning semantics: pinned-to-route (sticky whenever you open that route), pinned-to-account (cross-route), or ephemeral (session only). We should surface that when you hover.
Ryan: From infra side, we need to think telemetry: each pill toggle will fire analytics events. We'll get explosion of events if people toggle a lot. Suggest debounce + aggregate events per session.
Anika: Good call. Example event payload idea: `{ action: 'filter_toggled', filter_type: 'model', filter_value: 'gpt-4o', scope: 'route', session_id }`
Jess: For saved compact views, do we reuse existing saved-queries API or add a new light endpoint? Saved-queries is heavy (has ACLs, sharing, snapshots). Maybe a /views/quick endpoint that reuses model + route ids but simpler.
Tim: Internal API debate: should analytics return metrics keyed by routeId or modelVariantId when showing per-route+per-model columns? If route maps to many model variants, returning both might be heavy.
Ryan: I'd vote returning a top-level routeMetrics array and nested modelMetrics only when `expand_models=true`. Default stays compact. That keeps payload small.
Anika: That aligns with the UI — default compact table with a small model badge; click to expand models in-line. Also supports streaming expand without reloading.
Jess: UX question: filter precedence. If user pins a model to a route and then selects a global model filter, which wins? I think last-applied should win with a visual note: "Route pin overrides global".
Tim: Implementation-wise, server should resolve precedence and return an explicit `effective_filters` object in the view payload so the frontend doesn't have to recompute. Saves bugs.
Ryan: Telemetry event plan: emit `view_opened` with `effective_filters`, `pinned_count`, and `view_source` (user, team, shared). Aggregate server-side for retention.
Anika: Example light API proposal in pseudo: ```GET /api/console/quick-views?route_id=rt_123&expand_models=false response: { view_id, effective_filters: [{type: 'model', value: 'redwood-8bit', scope: 'route'}], routeMetrics: [{route_id: 'rt_123', rps: 12.3, avg_latency_ms: 142}], modelMetrics: [] }```
Jess: That looks clean. For save/share: quick view can be saved into saved-queries but as a 'compact' subtype. We can add `subtype: compact` to keep indexing separate.
Tim: Also think about permissions: team-shared compact views should be discoverable in the saved views dropdown. Keep ACLs consistent with saved-queries.
Ryan: One more ops note: adding pill toggles could create more demand on per-route endpoints (more filter combos). We should add a caching layer keyed by filter hash and TTL short (30s) to reduce load.
Anika: Nice. For UI: small keyboard shortcuts to toggle shelf pills (e.g., type `/` then 'm' for model) would make power users happy.
Jess: Love that. Action items: 1) Ryan to prototype server payload with `expand_models` flag (ETA 3 days). 2) Tim to spec `effective_filters` and precedence rules (ETA 2 days). 3) Anika/Jess to mock compact shelf UX and pin states (ETA 1 week). 4) Add telemetry debounce plan in infra doc.
